title.en: Stories of sharing: yoga, chilli, sugar, marigolds and cows

text.en: Long ago chilli plants grew only in South America. 400 to 500 years ago Portuguese travellers brought chillies to India and they entered Indian kitchens.

Yoga has been practised in India for over 3,000 years to keep the body healthy and the mind peaceful. Travellers and teachers shared it with the world. In 2014 the United Nations declared 21 June the International Day of Yoga.
Chilli: before chillies, India used black pepper to spice food. Chillies found new soil and a new climate, and now we cannot imagine our food without them. Potatoes, tomatoes, peanuts and cashews have similar stories.
Sugar: people elsewhere used honey for sweetness. In India the method of making jaggery from sugarcane juice was discovered, and later sugar. The knowledge spread by trade and travel. Rice, mangoes and bananas travelled too.
Marigold: a flower from Mexico that came to India and became part of temples, homes, weddings and Diwali. Both Indian and Mexican cultures use it in celebrations.
Cows: Portuguese traders took Indian cows to Brazil. They were strong, gave good milk and tolerated the weather. Today over three-fourths of Brazil's milk comes from the Gir, Kankrej and Ongole breeds.
Indian dyes like indigo coloured clothes in Africa and Europe. The deep blue was so special that it was once used only by royals.
Zero was first written down in India, and it helped people around the world do mathematics better. Chess and snakes and ladders started in India.
Spices like pepper and cardamom were called black gold and traders travelled far to get them. Paper came to India from China, and Arab traders brought dates and lemons and took back rice and cloth.
Activity: trace the journey of chilli on a globe with coloured string, and find the story of the potato, tomato, peanut or cashew.

problem.en: Which things travelled to India and which from India?

text.en: Chilli and marigold came to India.
Yoga, sugar and Gir cows went out.
Many things travelled both ways.

prompt.en: What do these stories tell us?

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking all our foods began in India

points.en: Chilli came to India, sugar and yoga went out.
The world shares ideas, food and plants.
